hyps.why: Raising an already large learning rate causes divergence and a sharp accuracy drop.
Very small learning rates leave the network undertrained in 243 epochs, so increasing them helps substantially.
Stepping back from a divergent learning rate recovers large amounts of accuracy.
Small batches produce noisy gradients, so larger steps destabilize training more.
With a tiny learning rate, fewer updates per epoch from larger batches worsen undertraining.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise and stabilize training under aggressive learning rates.
Increasing an already strong L2 penalty pushes the model into underfitting.
Relaxing excessive regularization restores capacity and accuracy.
Narrow networks are capacity-limited, so widening helps most there.
Deeper networks are more prone to instability under large learning rates.
